did_you_know.text: The list includes 'the Hittite' among Canaanite peoples — scholars debate whether this refers to the same people as the Anatolian Hittite empire.
'One voice' signals a coalition of kings — a temporary union of city-states against a common threat.
Wineskins were leather bags for liquids; when old they tend to split — a detail that helped make the Gibeonites' disguise believable.
The word 'nikudim' describing their bread has multiple interpretations — translations render it as dry, spotted, or damaged by insects/mildew.
Requesting a treaty while claiming to come 'from a far country' was a legal and religious tactic — cities sought protection instead of total destruction.
Saying they did not ask 'the mouth of the LORD' highlights that the leaders acted without spiritual consultation — a factor that shaped what followed.
The leaders' oath in the name of the LORD shows how binding public oaths were in ancient society.
The curse 'you are cursed' here does not mean execution but a reduction to servant status — in the Bible curses can become sentences of public service.
The phrase 'to this day' is a biblical formula indicating that an institution or situation continued into the writer's own time.
